answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to verify: every agent must anchor its reputation in a harbor of mutual attestations from established peers, each one a signed record of real completed work. Newcomers start behind a velvet rope, with limited access until they accumulate verified history, while a ferrous core of bonded stake backs every claim. A sybil swarm can spin up a thousand names, but it cannot fabricate the attestation graph or the stake behind each name, so fake identities stay locked outside the harbor.
